correctness.rationale: For every odd n>=3, antipodal quotient graph FQ_n admits canonical identification of its classes with the EVEN vectors of Q_n: each antipodal pair contains exactly one even vector. Each open neighborhood of FQ_n is the projection of the open neighborhood of one ODD cube vertex, with even parity representatives; hence the face lists coincide and N(FQ_n) is SIMPLICIALLY ISOMORPHIC to one parity component of N(Q_n). Independently checked entire facet systems for n=3,5,7. In the submitted proof high-dimensional face intersections are 0 or 2, facetwise free-face collapses reduce to a 2-complex, an antipodal square-complex covering plus odd deck path kills even pi1 (Matsushita), and Euler gives chi=2^{n-3}(n^2-5n+8); the resulting simply connected two-complex is wedge^{chi-1} S^2. Independent finite cases corroborate only; the cited theoretical collapse/topology prove all n.
residual_risks: Proof of all odd n requires published graph fundamental-group theorem; finite cases alone do not establish arbitrary n.

originality.rationale: Every odd-dimensional folded-cube quotient has its neighborhood complex canonically simplicially ISOMORPHIC to a single parity component of the ordinary n-cube neighborhood complex, using the unique even representative of each antipodal pair. A distinct published theorem already establishes this component has precisely the same 2-sphere wedge multiplicity mu_n for ALL n>=4 (hence all odd n>=5). The n=3 case is K4, whose neighborhood complex is the elementary tetrahedron boundary S². Thus the assigned entire odd-n family is a corollary of broader published coverage, not new theorem.
